# Root module manifest

Source: https://inditextech.github.io/kumoss/stable/main/reference/root-module-manifest/

A Terraform root module rarely runs on its code alone: its providers need to know which subscription, project, account or compartment to work in, and its input variables without a default need values. Kumoss asks for these once per root module, keeps the answers in a **manifest**, `kumoss.yaml`, committed inside the module, and reuses them on every later session.

## What Kumoss reads from the module

Before a session runs, the core inspects the root module statically with HashiCorp’s `terraform-config-inspect` (bundled in the core image; no `init`, no provider download) and scans its variable-definition files:

**Providers** — every entry of the module’s `required_providers`, identified by its Terraform provider **type**: the last segment of its source address (`azurerm` for `hashicorp/azurerm`, `google`, `aws`, `oci`, `kubernetes`, `vsphere`, `random`, `helm`…​). A module may use several, and every one of them is part of the session. Nobody picks a provider in the wizard any more.

**Variables** — each `variable` block’s name, type, description, and whether it is required (no default) or `sensitive`.

**Var files** — `terraform.tfvars` and **.auto.tfvars at the module’s top level, which Terraform loads on its own, and any other `.tfvars` or `.tfvars.json` file up to three directories below the module (`envs/dev.tfvars`), which are *optional**: the user may pick them,
and each run passes them as `-var-file` in the order picked, so
Terraform reads them itself, fresh on every command. Kumoss only
reads which variables a file sets. Subdirectories that are modules
themselves, hidden directories and symlinks are skipped.

A configuration with errors is reported as `422` rather than guessed at.

## Scopes

Four providers have a **scope**, the place their resources live in, and need one before a session can run:

| Provider | Scope | Sent to the IaC sidecar as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `azurerm` | subscription id | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` in `env` |
| `google` | project id | `GOOGLE_PROJECT` in `env` |
| `aws` | account id | `aws_account_id` in `vars` |
| `oci` | compartment OCID | `compartment_ocid` in `vars` |

The user answers each scope once, in the inputs form; it is saved in the manifest. The core turns it into the environment variable of every command the session runs, or into an input variable of every `plan` and `import`, sent last so no configured value overrides it. Because the core fills `aws_account_id` and `compartment_ocid` from the scope, those two variables are never asked for. Every other provider has no scope and runs on whatever the IaC sidecar’s ambient credentials and configuration select. See [Environment and input variables](../api/iac/#environment-and-input-variables) and [Terraform providers](../terraform-providers/).

## The manifest file

The manifest is a YAML file named `kumoss.yaml` (configurable with [`paths.manifest_filename`](../configuration/#config-paths)) in the root module’s directory:

```
# Managed by Kumoss: the inputs this Terraform root module is configured with.
# Sensitive values are never stored here, only their names.
version: "1"
project_identifier: sistemas-kumoss-rsg-esc1-dev
fingerprint: sha256:<hex>
providers:
  - name: azurerm
    source: hashicorp/azurerm
    version_constraints: ["~> 4.0"]
var_files: [envs/dev.tfvars]
variables:
  - name: region
    value: westeurope
  - name: db_password
    sensitive: true
scopes:
  - provider: azurerm
    scope_id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The layout version, `"1"`. |
| `project_identifier` | Optional. What the user named the repository when it was not its URL (a name the [mapping sidecar](../api/mapping/) resolved), as recorded by the latest session that saved the manifest. Written only when the session has one. Informational: it is refreshed on every save and never makes the manifest drift. See [Project identifier](#project-identifier). |
| `fingerprint` | A digest of what the user answers for: the providers and their constraints, each variable’s name, type, required and sensitive flags, which variables the auto-loaded files set, and which optional var files exist. Descriptions, defaults and the contents of optional var files are left out, so editing them never triggers a question. |
| `providers` | The module’s `required_providers` when the manifest was written. |
| `var_files` | The optional var files picked, in the order they are passed. |
| `variables` | The user’s answers. Plain values are stored as given, in any JSON type. Sensitive ones carry only `sensitive: true`; their value is kept elsewhere (see [Where values and secrets live](#where-values-live)). |
| `scopes` | One `{provider, scope_id}` entry per scoped provider of the module. |

The file is committed by a session on its branch, together with the session’s other changes, and reaches the default branch when the session’s pull request is merged. Only `version` and `fingerprint` are required; every other key is optional. Reading is strict about what is there: the file may be edited by hand, so a known key with the wrong type or shape is reported (`422`) rather than guessed, and a sensitive variable written with a value is refused with an instruction to remove it and rotate the secret. Unknown keys, at any level, are ignored, so a newer layout can add keys without breaking older readers; they are not kept when Kumoss saves the file.

### Project identifier

A repository can be named by a **project identifier**, such as `sistemas-kumoss-rsg-esc1-dev`, that the mapping sidecar resolves to its URL. When the session’s first call carries one (the `project_identifier` field of the [Core API](../api/core/#infrastructure-as-code)), the session writes it to the manifest. Every session’s first call records its own identifier: when it differs from the manifest’s, or the session has none and the manifest does, the manifest is saved even if nothing else changed, and a session without one removes the key. It is not part of the `fingerprint`, so the probe never reports `drifted` or `needs_input` because of it.

## Where values and secrets live

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Plain variable values, picked var files, scopes | `kumoss.yaml`, committed in the repository next to the module. |
| Sensitive variable values | One JSON object per root module in Kumoss’s object storage (the artifacts bucket, `storage.bucket`), at `manifests/<sha256 of repository and module path>/secrets.json`. The key does not depend on the branch or the clone. Object storage is not a secret manager: confidentiality rests on the bucket’s access policy and server-side encryption. |
| Values at run time | Sent to the IaC sidecar on `plan` and `import`: the picked var files as `var_files`, in the order picked, and the answers as `vars`, which win. The sidecar writes `vars` to an owner-only temporary file outside the workspace for the duration of the command. See [Environment and input variables](../api/iac/#environment-and-input-variables). |

A variable declared `sensitive` in the code is always stored as a secret. Any other variable can be marked secret by the user in the inputs form (`sensitive: true` in the API). Probe responses and session read models never contain values.

Provider **credentials** are not manifest inputs: they stay in the IaC sidecar’s environment, or an IaC service implementation picks them by the session’s [project identifier](#project-identifier).

## Before a session: the probe

`POST /api/v1/manifest/probe` with `repo_uri` and `root_module_path` reads the module on the repository’s **default branch** and reports what a session on it would need. It never writes anything.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `not_found` (no manifest yet), `up_to_date`, or `drifted` (the module changed since the manifest was written, or something the manifest relies on is gone). |
| `needs_input` | Whether the first session call must carry answers. True when a value, a var file selection or a scope is missing, and on a first setup when the module has optional var files to choose from. |
| `missing_variables` | Required variables nothing covers — no default, no auto-loaded file, no picked var file, no saved answer — and sensitive variables whose stored value is gone. Each with its name, type, description, and `required`/`sensitive` flags. |
| `selectable_var_files` | The optional var files, each with `selected` and `sets` (the variables it sets; picking it answers those). |
| `missing_var_files` | Picked var files that no longer exist; a new selection is needed. |
| `missing_scopes` | Scoped providers with no scope yet, as `{provider, source}`. |
| `provider_changes` | Providers added, removed or re-constrained since the manifest was written. |

## The first session call

The answers ride on the first `generate`, `drift` or `import` call, in `manifest`:

```
{
  "q": "Add a private storage account for application logs",
  "repo_uri": "https://github.com/acme/infra.git",
  "root_module_path": "environments/dev",
  "manifest": {
    "variables": [
      {"name": "db_password", "value": "s3cr3t"},
      {"name": "region", "value": "westeurope", "sensitive": false}
    ],
    "var_files": ["envs/dev.tfvars"],
    "scopes": {"azurerm": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}
  }
}
```

When the probe says `needs_input: false`, `manifest` is omitted. Either way the session, right after cloning:

1. inspects the module again and reconciles it with the committed manifest and the answers;
2. derives the session’s provider/scope pairs and has the [authorization sidecar](../api/authz/) evaluate each of them, **before anything is saved**;
3. stores the secret values, writes `kumoss.yaml` and commits it to the session branch (nothing is committed when nothing changed);
4. records the providers and scopes on the session, where the session read models show them as `providers: [{name, scope_id}]`.

If something is still missing, or an answer is invalid (unknown variable or provider, a value of the wrong shape, a var file that cannot be selected), the session ends `FAILED` with the reason — for example `The root module needs values for db_password. Probe it with POST /v1/manifest/probe and send the answers in manifest.` — and nothing is saved. Iteration calls cannot carry `manifest`: they reuse the providers, scopes and inputs set up at the first call.

## In the web application

The wizard asks for the request, the repository URL and the root module, then probes the module ("Checking what the root module needs…​"). When nothing is needed the session starts straight away. Otherwise it shows the inputs form, "This root module needs a few values", with up to three groups:

- **Scopes** — one field per provider in `missing_scopes`, labeled in the provider’s terms (Subscription ID, Project ID, Account ID, Compartment OCID).
- **Values** — one field per missing variable, typed after the declaration (JSON for lists, maps and objects), with a **Secret** toggle; a variable declared sensitive is always a secret.
- **Variable files** — the optional var files, picked in order. A variable that a picked file sets can be left empty.

The answers go with the session’s first call. They are asked once: the next session on the same module finds them in the manifest — once the pull request carrying `kumoss.yaml` has been merged into the default branch, which is what the probe reads.

## When the module changes

The manifest is checked against the code at the start of every session (never on iteration calls):

- **Nothing to ask** — a provider bump, a removed variable, a new variable with a default, a variable newly declared `sensitive` (its plain value moves to the secret store), a provider that no longer needs a scope — the session updates the manifest by itself and commits it with its changes. The probe reports `drifted` with `needs_input: false`.
- **Something to ask** — a new required variable, a new scoped provider, a picked var file that was deleted, or a secret whose stored value is gone (asked again rather than silently replaced by a default) — the probe reports `needs_input: true` and the wizard asks only for that.

A module that has no manifest and needs nothing (no required variable, no scoped provider, no optional var file) is set up silently on its first session.

## Related pages

- [Core API](../api/core/#manifest) for the probe route and the `manifest` request field.
- [Terraform providers](../terraform-providers/) for the credentials each provider needs in the IaC sidecar.
- [Prompt registry](../prompt-registry/#runtime-lookup) for how the module’s providers select the prompts a session uses.
- [Compliance policy](../compliance-policy/#input) for how the module’s provider type names reach the Rego policy as `input.kumoss.providers`.
- [Upgrade notes](../../guides/upgrade-notes/) for what changed when providers moved to the module.

# End-to-end flow

Source: https://inditextech.github.io/kumoss/stable/main/architecture/end-to-end-flow/

One generate session, from request to applied infrastructure, in ten phases across five sequence diagrams. Each diagram shows only the participants its phases use; the [legend](#legend) lists them and the arrow conventions.

Every step that changes state or blocks progress belongs to the control gates on purpose: **models propose, code decides.**

## Phases 1 and 2: request and session

![Kumoss request flow, phases 1 to 4: request, identity, session, then filter and compose](../../_images/flow-phases-1-4.png)

Pan, zoom, search, follow a message, switch themes. [Open in a new tab](../../_attachments/flow-phases-1-4.html)

/* Progressive enhancement for the block above. Guarded so that a page holding
   several diagrams runs this once, and deferred to DOMContentLoaded because a
   parse-time script cannot yet see the diagrams below it. */
(function () {
  if (window.__archifyEmbed) return
  window.__archifyEmbed = true

  /* The viewer's own interactive chrome. Its toolbar and zoom bar are
     position:fixed, so they always reach the bottom of whatever viewport the
     iframe gives them -- measuring them would make the height measurement
     below a fixpoint that can never shrink. Same selector list as
     docs/diagrams/capture-png.mjs, which hides them instead; here they stay
     visible and are only excluded from the measurement. */
  var CHROME = '.toolbar, .diagram-nav, .focus-chip, .guided-views, .archify-toast, .no-print'

  var style = document.createElement('style')
  style.textContent = [
    '.archify-actions{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.35rem .9rem;align-items:baseline;',
    'margin-block:-.65rem 1.5rem;font-size:.875rem;line-height:1.5}',
    '.archify-hint{opacity:.72}',
    '.archify-frame{width:100%;border:0;display:block}',
    /* A viewer is ~800KB and takes real time to arrive, so it loads out of
       the way while the still stays on screen, and is only swapped in once
       it has something to show. Off-screen rather than display:none: a
       display:none iframe has no viewport, so the application inside would
       not lay out, and revealing it would show an empty frame anyway --
       which is the whole failure this avoids. */
    '.archify-frame[data-archify-loading]{position:absolute;left:-99999px;top:0}',
    /* Only while the viewer is live. The still image is centred by the theme
       inside the narrower .imageblock; the frame is centred by this margin
       inside the wider one. */
    '.imageblock.archify-live{margin-inline:auto}',
    /* The theme insets an image block's contents by 40px, which puts the
       diagram 40px right of every heading and paragraph on the page. Those
       do line up with each other: a heading's box starts 64px further left
       than its text, because the theme carves that gutter with a negative
       margin and an equal padding to hold the hover anchor. So the column
       edge is where the text sits, and the diagram was the one thing off it.
       Dropped on both forms, so activating a block does not shift it. */
    '.imageblock.archify-block > .content{padding-inline:0}',
  ].join('')
  document.head.appendChild(style)

  /* The .imageblock wrapper is what escapes the 820px .sectionbody cap
     (`width: min(calc(var(--content-max-width)*1.25), var(--doc-inset-cap))`),
     so the viewer is swapped in inside it rather than in place of it. */
  function blockFor (actions) {
    var el = actions.previousElementSibling
    while (el && !el.classList.contains('imageblock')) el = el.previousElementSibling
    return el
  }

  /* Width is the only lever on how large the viewer draws: its SVG comes out
     at roughly 0.9x the viewport width it is given, and viewport height barely
     moves it. But --doc-inset-cap holds .imageblock at 1025px however wide the
     window gets, which on a large display leaves the whole right half of the
     article column unused. Track the column instead, so a 2560px screen gets
     a 1490px frame rather than the still's 945px. */
  function columnWidth (block) {
    var column = block.closest('.doc')
    return column ? column.clientWidth : 0
  }

  function widen (block) {
    var width = columnWidth(block)
    if (width) block.style.width = width + 'px'
  }

  /* Height of the real content, which is not the same as the document height:
     the viewer is a full-viewport application, so both scrollHeight and body
     height just echo back the height we set. Measure the lowest visible
     content edge instead, ignoring the fixed chrome. */
  function contentHeight (frame) {
    var doc = frame.contentDocument
    if (!doc) return 0
    var view = doc.defaultView
    var root = doc.querySelector('.container') || doc.body
    var nodes = root.querySelectorAll('*')
    var bottom = 0
    for (var i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) {
      var node = nodes[i]
      var computed = view.getComputedStyle(node)
      if (computed.display === 'none' || computed.visibility === 'hidden' || computed.opacity === '0') continue
      if (computed.position === 'fixed' || node.closest(CHROME)) continue
      var rect = node.getBoundingClientRect()
      if (!rect.width || !rect.height) continue
      bottom = Math.max(bottom, rect.bottom)
    }
    return bottom ? Math.ceil(bottom + 24) : 0
  }

  /* A wider frame makes the viewer draw a larger diagram, which makes it
     taller, which is the measurement that sized the frame. Settle it over a
     few bounded passes instead of assuming one is enough, and stop once the
     change is not worth another reflow.

     A measurement of zero means the viewer has not laid itself out yet, not
     that it never will: each one is a whole application, and end-to-end-flow
     loads five of them at once over a cold cache. Keep waiting, because
     giving up here strands the frame at its seeded height for good. */
  function fit (frame, pass, waits) {
    var height = contentHeight(frame)
    if (!height) {
      if ((waits || 0) < 60) setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, pass, (waits || 0) + 1) }, 250)
      return
    }
    var current = parseInt(frame.style.height, 10) || 0
    if (Math.abs(height - current) < 8) return
    frame.style.height = height + 'px'
    if ((pass || 0) < 3) setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, (pass || 0) + 1, 0) }, 250)
  }

  /* Replaces one still with its viewer, then calls `done` to free the slot for
     the next one -- on load, or on the breaker below, whichever comes first.

     The still stays on screen for the whole download. An earlier version put
     the frame in place the moment it was created, which left a blank grey
     panel where the diagram had been until ~800KB arrived: on a fast static
     server that is a flicker, on anything slower it is the whole reading
     experience. So the frame loads off-screen, at the size it is about to
     occupy, and the swap happens in one synchronous block. */
  function activate (actions, done) {
    var block = blockFor(actions)
    if (!block || block.classList.contains('archify-live')) return done()
    var content = block.firstElementChild || block
    var still = content.querySelector('img')

    var frame = document.createElement('iframe')
    frame.className = 'archify-frame'
    frame.title = actions.dataset.archifyTitle || 'Interactive diagram'
    /* Load it at the size it will be revealed at, so the viewer lays out for
       the real column and appearing costs no second reflow. Antora writes no
       width/height on the still, so one that has not decoded yet measures
       zero: fall back to a nominal height rather than a collapsed frame. */
    var seed = still ? Math.round(still.getBoundingClientRect().height) : 0
    frame.style.height = (seed > 120 ? seed : 620) + 'px'
    frame.style.width = (columnWidth(block) || block.clientWidth || 900) + 'px'
    frame.setAttribute('data-archify-loading', '')

    /* Everything that makes the frame visible, in one go, so no intermediate
       state is ever painted. The frame is never moved in the DOM --
       re-inserting an iframe reloads it, which would throw away the wait --
       so the still is removed around it instead. */
    function reveal () {
      frame.removeAttribute('data-archify-loading')
      frame.style.width = ''
      /* .imageblock is display:flex and .content is a shrink-wrapping flex
         item: the image sized it by its own intrinsic width, but an iframe
         has none, so .content would collapse to the UA's 300px iframe default
         and the frame's width:100% would resolve against an indefinite
         container. Pin .content to the flex container's width so the
         percentage has something definite to resolve against. */
      content.style.width = '100%'
      block.classList.add('archify-live')
      widen(block)
      for (var i = content.children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        if (content.children[i] !== frame) content.children[i].remove()
      }
    }

    /* One viewer loads at a time, so a frame that never fires load would hold
       the queue for good and strand every diagram below it as a still.
       Release the slot after a generous wait; this frame still reveals itself
       if it turns up late. */
    var settled = false
    function settle () {
      if (settled) return
      settled = true
      done()
    }
    setTimeout(settle, 15000)

    frame.addEventListener('load', function () {
      /* The viewer repeats its own title as an <h1> above the diagram, and
         every page that embeds one already carries that line as the section
         heading right above the frame. Two of the same sentence is one too
         many, and at column width the repeat wraps onto a second line and
         runs into the viewer's own toolbar. Hidden here rather than removed
         from the specification: a title is required there, and the "Open in a
         new tab" page has no surrounding heading to make it redundant. Same
         document, same origin, so this is a stylesheet and not a message. */
      var inner = frame.contentDocument
      if (inner) {
        var hide = inner.createElement('style')
        hide.textContent = '.container > .header{display:none}'
        inner.head.appendChild(hide)
      }

      /* `load` means the viewer's assets arrived and its scripts ran, not that
         it has drawn: the SVG appears in a later layout pass. Revealing on
         load alone shows the viewer's own empty panel for a frame or two, so
         wait for the drawing to exist -- briefly, and then reveal anyway,
         because a viewer that never draws must not keep the still forever. */
      var tries = 0
      ;(function ready () {
        var drawn = false
        try { drawn = !!(inner && inner.querySelector('svg')) } catch (e) { drawn = true }
        if (!drawn && ++tries <= 20) return void setTimeout(ready, 100)

        reveal()
        settle()

        /* Only now is the frame in the flow at its final width, so this is
           where the height measurement belongs. */
        setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, 0) }, 400)
        var width = 0
        new ResizeObserver(function () {
          /* Width only: observing our own height would loop against fit(). */
          var next = Math.round(frame.getBoundingClientRect().width)
          if (next === width) return
          width = next
          fit(frame, 0)
        }).observe(frame)
      })()
    })

    content.appendChild(frame)
    frame.src = actions.dataset.archifySrc
  }

  /* A page can hold five of these and each is a whole application of roughly
     800KB, so they are loaded strictly one at a time.

     Serial, not merely staggered. An earlier version started one every 900ms,
     which on a slow origin simply put all five in flight together: a browser
     opens about six connections per origin, five long downloads take nearly
     all of them, and the next click on the navigation sidebar gets no socket
     at all. That is not a slow page, it is a page that has stopped answering
     -- the network panel shows the navigation cancelled with zero bytes
     transferred. One viewer at a time bounds the cost to a single connection
     however slow the origin is, and the reader keeps a still until its
     replacement is ready, so nothing is lost by waiting.

     Proximity decides the order and never whether. Two earlier versions let it
     decide whether, and both stranded the lower diagrams as stills for good:
     the reader saw a tiny illegible image where a viewer should be. The cause
     outlives either mechanism. Antora writes no width or height on a still, so
     every image reflows everything below it as it decodes -- which means a
     block can be carried into range with no event to announce it. An
     IntersectionObserver's one-shot entry arrives against a position the block
     no longer holds; a rect read on scroll is never stale, but nothing reads it
     once the reader stops scrolling. Working through the whole queue removes
     that class of failure instead of widening the window it hides in: being
     near a diagram only brings it forward. */
  function enhance () {
    var pending = []
    var actions = document.querySelectorAll('.archify-actions[data-archify-src]')
    for (var i = 0; i < actions.length; i++) {
      var block = blockFor(actions[i])
      if (!block) continue
      /* Marks the blocks this script owns, so the stylesheet above can reach
         them while they are still stills. */
      block.classList.add('archify-block')
      pending.push(actions[i])
    }
    if (!pending.length) return

    var queued = false
    var running = false

    function stop () {
      window.removeEventListener('scroll', schedule)
      window.removeEventListener('resize', schedule)
    }

    /* Leaving the page ends the queue. Without this, a click on the navigation
       sidebar races a pump that is about to start another ~800KB viewer: the
       browser asks for the next document while this page opens one more
       connection for a viewer nobody will ever see, and on a slow origin the
       navigation is what waits. The reader reads that as a page that has
       stopped answering. Nothing below needs the queue once the document is
       on its way out. */
    window.addEventListener('pagehide', function () {
      pending.length = 0
      stop()
    })

    /* One observer for the whole column, not one per diagram. Every live block
       tracks the same element, so five separate observers on it did the same
       work five times over on every resize. */
    var column = document.querySelector('.doc')
    if (column) {
      new ResizeObserver(function () {
        var live = document.querySelectorAll('.imageblock.archify-live')
        for (var i = 0; i < live.length; i++) widen(live[i])
      }).observe(column)
    }

    /* The one place a viewer is ever started. Nothing else calls activate, so
       there is exactly one download in flight no matter what triggers a
       pump -- scroll, resize, or the previous one finishing. */
    function pump () {
      if (running || !pending.length) return
      running = true
      activate(pending.shift(), function () {
        running = false
        if (pending.length) setTimeout(pump, 250)
        else stop()
      })
    }

    /* Reorders what is left so anything the reader can nearly see goes next,
       and never activates anything itself. A diagram already passed keeps its
       place in the queue: the saving worth having is not loading five viewers
       at once, not reclaiming one that has scrolled off the top. */
    function promote () {
      queued = false
      var visible = []
      var rest = []
      for (var i = 0; i < pending.length; i++) {
        var block = blockFor(pending[i])
        var close = block && block.getBoundingClientRect().top <= window.innerHeight + 400
        ;(close ? visible : rest).push(pending[i])
      }
      pending = visible.concat(rest)
      pump()
    }

    function schedule () {
      if (queued) return
      queued = true
      requestAnimationFrame(promote)
    }

    window.addEventListener('scroll', schedule, { passive: true })
    window.addEventListener('resize', schedule)
    promote()
  }

  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enhance)
  else enhance()
})()

Messages 1 to 13; the diagram also covers phases 3 and 4.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Request | The wizard posts repository URL, root module path, request text and, when the module needed them, the answers to its inputs (`manifest`) to `POST /api/v1/iac/generate` with a bearer token. The root module path is one of the Terraform roots `POST /api/v1/repository/parse` found in a metadata-only clone (a `git ls-tree` heuristic over `.tf` directories), which also echoed what the user typed as `project_identifier`; the wizard sends that back too. Before posting, the wizard asked `POST /api/v1/manifest/probe` what the module needs and, only when something was missing, showed the inputs form. No provider or scope is sent: they come from the module itself. See [Root module manifest](../../reference/root-module-manifest/). |
| Identity and role | The authentication dependency validates the bearer JWT, or resolves the fixed local-developer identity when auth is disabled, and the role check requires `developer`: `401` or `403` otherwise. The authz sidecar is consulted later, once the module’s provider scopes are known (see the manifest step below). See [Authentication](#auth) and [Authorization and ownership](#authz). |
| Repository reachability | The URL must be `https://` with a host — SSH (`git@host:path`, `ssh://`), `git://`, `http://`, `file://` and local paths are rejected with `422` by a request-model validator. It may carry a userinfo username (the `<org>@` prefix of an Azure DevOps clone URL) but must not embed a password or token — also `422`, an empty `user:` password included. Then `git ls-remote` must succeed: unreachable, rejected or timed out → `400` with the fixed detail "Repository is not reachable or access was denied."; git’s own output goes only to the core log. A `project_identifier` other than the URL itself must then resolve to it through the mapping sidecar, or the call is `422` (a mapper error such as `404` is passed through). Either way no session is created. |
| Session creation | A session row owned by the caller is created, or an existing one resolved by `session_id` with ownership asserted; a round opens and the API answers `202 Accepted` with the session id. Everything from here runs as an in-process background task. |
| Progress stream | The UI subscribes to `GET /api/v1/events/subscribe/{session_id}` and receives status events every 4-5 seconds until a terminal status. |
| Guard, workspace, tracing | The runner takes the in-flight guard, an atomic compare-and-set on the session row. The `202` has already been sent, so a concurrent request is never refused with `409`: the runner that loses logs `runner not started: Session …​ already has an operation in flight` and returns without touching the session. It then clones into `/workspaces/<session>/<call>` on the volume shared with the iac sidecar, pushes the branch `Kumoss/YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS` (UTC), and installs the per-session Langfuse tracer. |
| Manifest and authorization | On a first call the runner inspects the root module, reconciles it with its committed `kumoss.yaml` and the call’s `manifest` answers, and derives the session’s provider/scope pairs. The authz sidecar is asked once per pair before anything is saved; a denial, or input still missing, fails the session there. Otherwise the secrets are stored, the manifest is written and committed to the session branch, and the pairs are recorded on the session. Iteration calls skip this and reuse the recorded pairs, authorized synchronously on the route. Every generate, drift or import call then loads the module’s var files and values for its Terraform runs; apply runs the pinned plan, which already has them. |

## Phases 3 and 4: filter and compose

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Request Filter Agent (`filtering`) | The small model, with read-only workspace tools, classifies the request against the `general/guidelines/requests` prompt. A change request proceeds; a question is answered in the conversation; an out-of-scope or ambiguous request is declined with a rationale. In the last two cases the round ends `uncompleted` and the user is invited to reformulate — the session itself stays usable. |
| Prompt Compositor | Two small-model passes select the relevant resource templates and abbreviations from the `resources_list` and `abbreviations` prompts of the module’s providers in Langfuse, then look for dependencies among them. The result is the round’s *conventions*, which every later agent is rendered with. |

## Phase 5: generate, validate, correct

Up to `orchestration.max_validation_iteration` generate-and-validate iterations: 5 in the shipped `config.yaml`, 8 built in.

![Kumoss request flow, phases 5 and 6: generate, validate, correct, then the implicit drift pre-check](../../_images/flow-phases-5-6.png)

Pan, zoom, search, follow a message, switch themes. [Open in a new tab](../../_attachments/flow-phases-5-6.html)

/* Progressive enhancement for the block above. Guarded so that a page holding
   several diagrams runs this once, and deferred to DOMContentLoaded because a
   parse-time script cannot yet see the diagrams below it. */
(function () {
  if (window.__archifyEmbed) return
  window.__archifyEmbed = true

  /* The viewer's own interactive chrome. Its toolbar and zoom bar are
     position:fixed, so they always reach the bottom of whatever viewport the
     iframe gives them -- measuring them would make the height measurement
     below a fixpoint that can never shrink. Same selector list as
     docs/diagrams/capture-png.mjs, which hides them instead; here they stay
     visible and are only excluded from the measurement. */
  var CHROME = '.toolbar, .diagram-nav, .focus-chip, .guided-views, .archify-toast, .no-print'

  var style = document.createElement('style')
  style.textContent = [
    '.archify-actions{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.35rem .9rem;align-items:baseline;',
    'margin-block:-.65rem 1.5rem;font-size:.875rem;line-height:1.5}',
    '.archify-hint{opacity:.72}',
    '.archify-frame{width:100%;border:0;display:block}',
    /* A viewer is ~800KB and takes real time to arrive, so it loads out of
       the way while the still stays on screen, and is only swapped in once
       it has something to show. Off-screen rather than display:none: a
       display:none iframe has no viewport, so the application inside would
       not lay out, and revealing it would show an empty frame anyway --

    }
    return bottom ? Math.ceil(bottom + 24) : 0
  }

  /* A wider frame makes the viewer draw a larger diagram, which makes it
     taller, which is the measurement that sized the frame. Settle it over a
     few bounded passes instead of assuming one is enough, and stop once the
     change is not worth another reflow.

     that it never will: each one is a whole application, and end-to-end-flow
     loads five of them at once over a cold cache. Keep waiting, because
     giving up here strands the frame at its seeded height for good. */

    if (!height) {
      if ((waits || 0) < 60) setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, pass, (waits || 0) + 1) }, 250)
      return
    }
    var current = parseInt(frame.style.height, 10) || 0
    if (Math.abs(height - current) < 8) return
    frame.style.height = height + 'px'
    if ((pass || 0) < 3) setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, (pass || 0) + 1, 0) }, 250)
  }

  /* Replaces one still with its viewer, then calls `done` to free the slot for
     the next one -- on load, or on the breaker below, whichever comes first.

     The still stays on screen for the whole download. An earlier version put
     the frame in place the moment it was created, which left a blank grey
     panel where the diagram had been until ~800KB arrived: on a fast static
     server that is a flicker, on anything slower it is the whole reading
     experience. So the frame loads off-screen, at the size it is about to
     occupy, and the swap happens in one synchronous block. */

    if (!block || block.classList.contains('archify-live')) return done()

    var still = content.querySelector('img')

    var frame = document.createElement('iframe')
    frame.className = 'archify-frame'
    frame.title = actions.dataset.archifyTitle || 'Interactive diagram'
    /* Load it at the size it will be revealed at, so the viewer lays out for
       the real column and appearing costs no second reflow. Antora writes no
       width/height on the still, so one that has not decoded yet measures
       zero: fall back to a nominal height rather than a collapsed frame. */

    frame.style.height = (seed > 120 ? seed : 620) + 'px'
    frame.style.width = (columnWidth(block) || block.clientWidth || 900) + 'px'
    frame.setAttribute('data-archify-loading', '')

       state is ever painted. The frame is never moved in the DOM --
       re-inserting an iframe reloads it, which would throw away the wait --
       so the still is removed around it instead. */
    function reveal () {
      frame.removeAttribute('data-archify-loading')
      frame.style.width = ''
      /* .imageblock is display:flex and .content is a shrink-wrapping flex
         item: the image sized it by its own intrinsic width, but an iframe
         has none, so .content would collapse to the UA's 300px iframe default
         and the frame's width:100% would resolve against an indefinite
         container. Pin .content to the flex container's width so the
         percentage has something definite to resolve against. */

      block.classList.add('archify-live')
      widen(block)
      for (var i = content.children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        if (content.children[i] !== frame) content.children[i].remove()
      }
    }

    /* One viewer loads at a time, so a frame that never fires load would hold
       the queue for good and strand every diagram below it as a still.
       Release the slot after a generous wait; this frame still reveals itself
       if it turns up late. */
    var settled = false
    function settle () {
      if (settled) return
      settled = true
      done()
    }
    setTimeout(settle, 15000)

    frame.addEventListener('load', function () {
      /* The viewer repeats its own title as an <h1> above the diagram, and
         every page that embeds one already carries that line as the section
         heading right above the frame. Two of the same sentence is one too
         many, and at column width the repeat wraps onto a second line and
         runs into the viewer's own toolbar. Hidden here rather than removed
         from the specification: a title is required there, and the "Open in a
         new tab" page has no surrounding heading to make it redundant. Same
         document, same origin, so this is a stylesheet and not a message. */
      var inner = frame.contentDocument
      if (inner) {
        var hide = inner.createElement('style')
        hide.textContent = '.container > .header{display:none}'
        inner.head.appendChild(hide)
      }

      /* `load` means the viewer's assets arrived and its scripts ran, not that
         it has drawn: the SVG appears in a later layout pass. Revealing on
         load alone shows the viewer's own empty panel for a frame or two, so
         wait for the drawing to exist -- briefly, and then reveal anyway,
         because a viewer that never draws must not keep the still forever. */
      var tries = 0
      ;(function ready () {
        var drawn = false
        try { drawn = !!(inner && inner.querySelector('svg')) } catch (e) { drawn = true }
        if (!drawn && ++tries <= 20) return void setTimeout(ready, 100)

        reveal()
        settle()

        /* Only now is the frame in the flow at its final width, so this is
           where the height measurement belongs. */
        setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, 0) }, 400)
        var width = 0
        new ResizeObserver(function () {
          /* Width only: observing our own height would loop against fit(). */
          var next = Math.round(frame.getBoundingClientRect().width)
          if (next === width) return
          width = next
          fit(frame, 0)
        }).observe(frame)
      })()
    })

    content.appendChild(frame)
    frame.src = actions.dataset.archifySrc
  }

  /* A page can hold five of these and each is a whole application of roughly
     800KB, so they are loaded strictly one at a time.

     Serial, not merely staggered. An earlier version started one every 900ms,
     which on a slow origin simply put all five in flight together: a browser
     opens about six connections per origin, five long downloads take nearly
     all of them, and the next click on the navigation sidebar gets no socket
     at all. That is not a slow page, it is a page that has stopped answering
     -- the network panel shows the navigation cancelled with zero bytes
     transferred. One viewer at a time bounds the cost to a single connection
     however slow the origin is, and the reader keeps a still until its
     replacement is ready, so nothing is lost by waiting.

     Proximity decides the order and never whether. Two earlier versions let it
     decide whether, and both stranded the lower diagrams as stills for good:
     the reader saw a tiny illegible image where a viewer should be. The cause
     outlives either mechanism. Antora writes no width or height on a still, so
     every image reflows everything below it as it decodes -- which means a
     block can be carried into range with no event to announce it. An
     IntersectionObserver's one-shot entry arrives against a position the block
     no longer holds; a rect read on scroll is never stale, but nothing reads it
     once the reader stops scrolling. Working through the whole queue removes
     that class of failure instead of widening the window it hides in: being
     near a diagram only brings it forward. */
  function enhance () {
    var pending = []
    var actions = document.querySelectorAll('.archify-actions[data-archify-src]')
    for (var i = 0; i < actions.length; i++) {
      var block = blockFor(actions[i])
      if (!block) continue
      /* Marks the blocks this script owns, so the stylesheet above can reach
         them while they are still stills. */
      block.classList.add('archify-block')
      pending.push(actions[i])
    }
    if (!pending.length) return

    var queued = false
    var running = false

    function stop () {
      window.removeEventListener('scroll', schedule)
      window.removeEventListener('resize', schedule)
    }

    /* Leaving the page ends the queue. Without this, a click on the navigation
       sidebar races a pump that is about to start another ~800KB viewer: the
       browser asks for the next document while this page opens one more
       connection for a viewer nobody will ever see, and on a slow origin the
       navigation is what waits. The reader reads that as a page that has
       stopped answering. Nothing below needs the queue once the document is
       on its way out. */
    window.addEventListener('pagehide', function () {
      pending.length = 0
      stop()
    })

    /* One observer for the whole column, not one per diagram. Every live block
       tracks the same element, so five separate observers on it did the same
       work five times over on every resize. */
    var column = document.querySelector('.doc')
    if (column) {
      new ResizeObserver(function () {
        var live = document.querySelectorAll('.imageblock.archify-live')
        for (var i = 0; i < live.length; i++) widen(live[i])
      }).observe(column)
    }

    /* The one place a viewer is ever started. Nothing else calls activate, so
       there is exactly one download in flight no matter what triggers a
       pump -- scroll, resize, or the previous one finishing. */
    function pump () {
      if (running || !pending.length) return
      running = true
      activate(pending.shift(), function () {
        running = false
        if (pending.length) setTimeout(pump, 250)
        else stop()
      })
    }

    /* Reorders what is left so anything the reader can nearly see goes next,
       and never activates anything itself. A diagram already passed keeps its
       place in the queue: the saving worth having is not loading five viewers
       at once, not reclaiming one that has scrolled off the top. */
    function promote () {
      queued = false
      var visible = []
      var rest = []
      for (var i = 0; i < pending.length; i++) {
        var block = blockFor(pending[i])
        var close = block && block.getBoundingClientRect().top <= window.innerHeight + 400
        ;(close ? visible : rest).push(pending[i])
      }
      pending = visible.concat(rest)
      pump()
    }

    function schedule () {
      if (queued) return
      queued = true
      requestAnimationFrame(promote)
    }

    window.addEventListener('scroll', schedule, { passive: true })
    window.addEventListener('resize', schedule)
    promote()
  }

  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enhance)
  else enhance()
})()

Messages 14 to 25; the diagram also covers phase 6.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Infrastructure Generation Agent (`generating`) | The main model edits Terraform files through the tool registry (read, write, list, ripgrep search, web search), confined to the session’s IaC root and bounded by `orchestration.max_tool_agent_executions` (40) model turns — the same bound every agent loop shares — and terminated by the sentinel `task_complete` tool. The guards that keep the loop inside its budget are described in [Agent tool loop](#agent-tool-loop). |
| Persist and push | Every changed or new file is uploaded as a code-change artifact and committed and pushed to the session branch, so the work is durable before validation starts. |
| Session Target Generator | The main model derives this round’s `-target` list from the branch’s diff history, so the plan covers what the round changed rather than the whole root module. |
| Validation (`validating`) | `init`, `validate` and `plan -out session.plan -target …​` are submitted to the iac sidecar as asynchronous jobs, each polled every `services.iac.job_poll_interval` seconds within `services.iac.job_timeout`. The engine (OpenTofu by default) runs against the shared workspace with the cloud credentials in `services/iac/.env`. |
| Correct or fail | Engine errors go back to the generation agent as the next query and the loop repeats. After `orchestration.max_validation_iteration` (5 shipped) failures the round ends `FAILED`, the branch keeps the last pushed attempt, and the session is [closed for good](#how-a-session-ends). |

## Phase 6: implicit drift pre-check

Runs on the targets validation has just produced, at most twice.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect the plan | Status `reconciling`. The core runs `show -json` on the plan artifact validation left in the workspace — the round’s own plan, never a second one — and inverts the `before`/`after` differences into "make the code match the infrastructure" operations, stored as a drift artifact. When the targets are already in sync the plan output is stored instead, as a plan artifact, so every iteration leaves one artifact behind. |
| Split and filter | The Drift Task Splitter (main model) turns the differences into plain-language operations, the Reconciliation Filter (small model) reads the branch’s `diff_history` and drops every operation that would merely undo the session’s own intended changes, and the Drift Exception Filter (small model) then drops every operation the providers' `drift_exceptions` rules cover, logging what it removed. |
| Decide | Genuine drift re-enters the generation loop in batches of `orchestration.drift_group_operations` (8), and the pre-check runs once more. If only the session’s own changes remain, or the plan is clean, the pre-check stops and the last plan is final. If genuine drift is still there after the second iteration, the round continues to the report anyway: a warning is logged and the drift is re-read from the last remediation batch’s plan, so the report and the pinned plan agree. A remediation batch that exhausts its own validation attempts fails the round instead. |

Full mechanism, including the fingerprint that makes reading an existing plan safe: [Drift detection and remediation](#drift).

![Kumoss request flow, phases 7 and 8: report and artifacts, then the independent compliance check](../../_images/flow-phases-7-8.png)

Pan, zoom, search, follow a message, switch themes. [Open in a new tab](../../_attachments/flow-phases-7-8.html)

/* Progressive enhancement for the block above. Guarded so that a page holding
   several diagrams runs this once, and deferred to DOMContentLoaded because a
   parse-time script cannot yet see the diagrams below it. */
(function () {
  if (window.__archifyEmbed) return
  window.__archifyEmbed = true

  /* The viewer's own interactive chrome. Its toolbar and zoom bar are
     position:fixed, so they always reach the bottom of whatever viewport the
     iframe gives them -- measuring them would make the height measurement
     below a fixpoint that can never shrink. Same selector list as
     docs/diagrams/capture-png.mjs, which hides them instead; here they stay
     visible and are only excluded from the measurement. */
  var CHROME = '.toolbar, .diagram-nav, .focus-chip, .guided-views, .archify-toast, .no-print'

  var style = document.createElement('style')
  style.textContent = [
    '.archify-actions{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.35rem .9rem;align-items:baseline;',
    'margin-block:-.65rem 1.5rem;font-size:.875rem;line-height:1.5}',
    '.archify-hint{opacity:.72}',
    '.archify-frame{width:100%;border:0;display:block}',
    /* A viewer is ~800KB and takes real time to arrive, so it loads out of
       the way while the still stays on screen, and is only swapped in once
       it has something to show. Off-screen rather than display:none: a
       display:none iframe has no viewport, so the application inside would
       not lay out, and revealing it would show an empty frame anyway --
       which is the whole failure this avoids. */
    '.archify-frame[data-archify-loading]{position:absolute;left:-99999px;top:0}',
    /* Only while the viewer is live. The still image is centred by the theme
       inside the narrower .imageblock; the frame is centred by this margin
       inside the wider one. */
    '.imageblock.archify-live{margin-inline:auto}',
    /* The theme insets an image block's contents by 40px, which puts the
       diagram 40px right of every heading and paragraph on the page. Those
       do line up with each other: a heading's box starts 64px further left
       than its text, because the theme carves that gutter with a negative
       margin and an equal padding to hold the hover anchor. So the column
       edge is where the text sits, and the diagram was the one thing off it.
       Dropped on both forms, so activating a block does not shift it. */
    '.imageblock.archify-block > .content{padding-inline:0}',
  ].join('')
  document.head.appendChild(style)

  /* The .imageblock wrapper is what escapes the 820px .sectionbody cap
     (`width: min(calc(var(--content-max-width)*1.25), var(--doc-inset-cap))`),
     so the viewer is swapped in inside it rather than in place of it. */
  function blockFor (actions) {
    var el = actions.previousElementSibling
    while (el && !el.classList.contains('imageblock')) el = el.previousElementSibling
    return el
  }

  /* Width is the only lever on how large the viewer draws: its SVG comes out
     at roughly 0.9x the viewport width it is given, and viewport height barely
     moves it. But --doc-inset-cap holds .imageblock at 1025px however wide the
     window gets, which on a large display leaves the whole right half of the
     article column unused. Track the column instead, so a 2560px screen gets
     a 1490px frame rather than the still's 945px. */
  function columnWidth (block) {
    var column = block.closest('.doc')
    return column ? column.clientWidth : 0
  }

  function widen (block) {
    var width = columnWidth(block)
    if (width) block.style.width = width + 'px'
  }

  /* Height of the real content, which is not the same as the document height:
     the viewer is a full-viewport application, so both scrollHeight and body
     height just echo back the height we set. Measure the lowest visible
     content edge instead, ignoring the fixed chrome. */
  function contentHeight (frame) {
    var doc = frame.contentDocument
    if (!doc) return 0
    var view = doc.defaultView
    var root = doc.querySelector('.container') || doc.body
    var nodes = root.querySelectorAll('*')
    var bottom = 0
    for (var i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) {
      var node = nodes[i]
      var computed = view.getComputedStyle(node)
      if (computed.display === 'none' || computed.visibility === 'hidden' || computed.opacity === '0') continue
      if (computed.position === 'fixed' || node.closest(CHROME)) continue
      var rect = node.getBoundingClientRect()
      if (!rect.width || !rect.height) continue
      bottom = Math.max(bottom, rect.bottom)
    }
    return bottom ? Math.ceil(bottom + 24) : 0
  }

  /* A wider frame makes the viewer draw a larger diagram, which makes it
     taller, which is the measurement that sized the frame. Settle it over a
     few bounded passes instead of assuming one is enough, and stop once the
     change is not worth another reflow.

     A measurement of zero means the viewer has not laid itself out yet, not
     that it never will: each one is a whole application, and end-to-end-flow
     loads five of them at once over a cold cache. Keep waiting, because
     giving up here strands the frame at its seeded height for good. */
  function fit (frame, pass, waits) {
    var height = contentHeight(frame)
    if (!height) {
      if ((waits || 0) < 60) setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, pass, (waits || 0) + 1) }, 250)
      return
    }
    var current = parseInt(frame.style.height, 10) || 0
    if (Math.abs(height - current) < 8) return
    frame.style.height = height + 'px'
    if ((pass || 0) < 3) setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, (pass || 0) + 1, 0) }, 250)
  }

  /* Replaces one still with its viewer, then calls `done` to free the slot for
     the next one -- on load, or on the breaker below, whichever comes first.

     The still stays on screen for the whole download. An earlier version put
     the frame in place the moment it was created, which left a blank grey
     panel where the diagram had been until ~800KB arrived: on a fast static
     server that is a flicker, on anything slower it is the whole reading
     experience. So the frame loads off-screen, at the size it is about to
     occupy, and the swap happens in one synchronous block. */
  function activate (actions, done) {
    var block = blockFor(actions)
    if (!block || block.classList.contains('archify-live')) return done()
    var content = block.firstElementChild || block
    var still = content.querySelector('img')

    var frame = document.createElement('iframe')
    frame.className = 'archify-frame'
    frame.title = actions.dataset.archifyTitle || 'Interactive diagram'
    /* Load it at the size it will be revealed at, so the viewer lays out for
       the real column and appearing costs no second reflow. Antora writes no
       width/height on the still, so one that has not decoded yet measures
       zero: fall back to a nominal height rather than a collapsed frame. */
    var seed = still ? Math.round(still.getBoundingClientRect().height) : 0
    frame.style.height = (seed > 120 ? seed : 620) + 'px'
    frame.style.width = (columnWidth(block) || block.clientWidth || 900) + 'px'
    frame.setAttribute('data-archify-loading', '')

    /* Everything that makes the frame visible, in one go, so no intermediate
       state is ever painted. The frame is never moved in the DOM --
       re-inserting an iframe reloads it, which would throw away the wait --
       so the still is removed around it instead. */
    function reveal () {
      frame.removeAttribute('data-archify-loading')
      frame.style.width = ''
      /* .imageblock is display:flex and .content is a shrink-wrapping flex
         item: the image sized it by its own intrinsic width, but an iframe
         has none, so .content would collapse to the UA's 300px iframe default
         and the frame's width:100% would resolve against an indefinite
         container. Pin .content to the flex container's width so the
         percentage has something definite to resolve against. */
      content.style.width = '100%'
      block.classList.add('archify-live')
      widen(block)
      for (var i = content.children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        if (content.children[i] !== frame) content.children[i].remove()
      }
    }

    /* One viewer loads at a time, so a frame that never fires load would hold
       the queue for good and strand every diagram below it as a still.
       Release the slot after a generous wait; this frame still reveals itself
       if it turns up late. */
    var settled = false
    function settle () {
      if (settled) return
      settled = true
      done()
    }
    setTimeout(settle, 15000)

    frame.addEventListener('load', function () {
      /* The viewer repeats its own title as an <h1> above the diagram, and
         every page that embeds one already carries that line as the section
         heading right above the frame. Two of the same sentence is one too
         many, and at column width the repeat wraps onto a second line and
         runs into the viewer's own toolbar. Hidden here rather than removed
         from the specification: a title is required there, and the "Open in a
         new tab" page has no surrounding heading to make it redundant. Same
         document, same origin, so this is a stylesheet and not a message. */
      var inner = frame.contentDocument
      if (inner) {
        var hide = inner.createElement('style')
        hide.textContent = '.container > .header{display:none}'
        inner.head.appendChild(hide)
      }

      /* `load` means the viewer's assets arrived and its scripts ran, not that
         it has drawn: the SVG appears in a later layout pass. Revealing on
         load alone shows the viewer's own empty panel for a frame or two, so
         wait for the drawing to exist -- briefly, and then reveal anyway,
         because a viewer that never draws must not keep the still forever. */
      var tries = 0
      ;(function ready () {
        var drawn = false
        try { drawn = !!(inner && inner.querySelector('svg')) } catch (e) { drawn = true }
        if (!drawn && ++tries <= 20) return void setTimeout(ready, 100)

        reveal()
        settle()

        /* Only now is the frame in the flow at its final width, so this is
           where the height measurement belongs. */
        setTimeout(function () { fit(frame, 0) }, 400)
        var width = 0
        new ResizeObserver(function () {
          /* Width only: observing our own height would loop against fit(). */
          var next = Math.round(frame.getBoundingClientRect().width)
          if (next === width) return
          width = next
          fit(frame, 0)
        }).observe(frame)
      })()
    })

    content.appendChild(frame)
    frame.src = actions.dataset.archifySrc
  }

  /* A page can hold five of these and each is a whole application of roughly
     800KB, so they are loaded strictly one at a time.

     Serial, not merely staggered. An earlier version started one every 900ms,
     which on a slow origin simply put all five in flight together: a browser
     opens about six connections per origin, five long downloads take nearly
     all of them, and the next click on the navigation sidebar gets no socket
     at all. That is not a slow page, it is a page that has stopped answering
     -- the network panel shows the navigation cancelled with zero bytes
     transferred. One viewer at a time bounds the cost to a single connection
     however slow the origin is, and the reader keeps a still until its
     replacement is ready, so nothing is lost by waiting.

     Proximity decides the order and never whether. Two earlier versions let it
     decide whether, and both stranded the lower diagrams as stills for good:
     the reader saw a tiny illegible image where a viewer should be. The cause
     outlives either mechanism. Antora writes no width or height on a still, so
     every image reflows everything below it as it decodes -- which means a
     block can be carried into range with no event to announce it. An
     IntersectionObserver's one-shot entry arrives against a position the block
     no longer holds; a rect read on scroll is never stale, but nothing reads it
     once the reader stops scrolling. Working through the whole queue removes
     that class of failure instead of widening the window it hides in: being
     near a diagram only brings it forward. */
  function enhance () {
    var pending = []
    var actions = document.querySelectorAll('.archify-actions[data-archify-src]')
    for (var i = 0; i < actions.length; i++) {
      var block = blockFor(actions[i])
      if (!block) continue
      /* Marks the blocks this script owns, so the stylesheet above can reach
         them while they are still stills. */
      block.classList.add('archify-block')
      pending.push(actions[i])
    }
    if (!pending.length) return

    var queued = false
    var running = false

    function stop () {
      window.removeEventListener('scroll', schedule)
      window.removeEventListener('resize', schedule)
    }

    /* Leaving the page ends the queue. Without this, a click on the navigation
       sidebar races a pump that is about to start another ~800KB viewer: the
       browser asks for the next document while this page opens one more
       connection for a viewer nobody will ever see, and on a slow origin the
       navigation is what waits. The reader reads that as a page that has
       stopped answering. Nothing below needs the queue once the document is
       on its way out. */
    window.addEventListener('pagehide', function () {
      pending.length = 0
      stop()
    })

    /* One observer for the whole column, not one per diagram. Every live block
       tracks the same element, so five separate observers on it did the same
       work five times over on every resize. */
    var column = document.querySelector('.doc')
    if (column) {
      new ResizeObserver(function () {
        var live = document.querySelectorAll('.imageblock.archify-live')
        for (var i = 0; i < live.length; i++) widen(live[i])
      }).observe(column)
    }

    /* The one place a viewer is ever started. Nothing else calls activate, so
       there is exactly one download in flight no matter what triggers a
       pump -- scroll, resize, or the previous one finishing. */
    function pump () {
      if (running || !pending.length) return
      running = true
      activate(pending.shift(), function () {
        running = false
        if (pending.length) setTimeout(pump, 250)
        else stop()
      })
    }

    /* Reorders what is left so anything the reader can nearly see goes next,
       and never activates anything itself. A diagram already passed keeps its
       place in the queue: the saving worth having is not loading five viewers
       at once, not reclaiming one that has scrolled off the top. */
    function promote () {
      queued = false
      var visible = []
      var rest = []
      for (var i = 0; i < pending.length; i++) {
        var block = blockFor(pending[i])
        var close = block && block.getBoundingClientRect().top <= window.innerHeight + 400
        ;(close ? visible : rest).push(pending[i])
      }
      pending = visible.concat(rest)
      pump()
    }

    function schedule () {
      if (queued) return
      queued = true
      requestAnimationFrame(promote)
    }

    window.addEventListener('scroll', schedule, { passive: true })
    window.addEventListener('resize', schedule)
    promote()
  }

  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enhance)
  else enhance()
})()

Messages 26 to 34; the diagram also covers phase 8.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Report Generator (`report`) | The main model turns the final plan into a JSON report: create, update, delete and recreate counts, detailed changes, an impact banner (`low`, `medium`, `high`) assigned with the `general/compliance/impact` criteria, and cost estimates. |
| Artifacts | Report, plans, drift JSON and code changes go to object storage under `sessions/<session>/rounds/<round>/`, where `<round>` is the round’s **database primary key**, not its ordinal in the session. The key patterns are `reports/<report type>-<token>.json`, `plans/plan-<token>.txt`, `plans/drift-<token>.txt` and `changes/<token>-<sanitized file name>`. Metadata goes to PostgreSQL; the UI receives presigned URLs. |

## Phase 8: compliance check

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance policy | With `orchestration.enable_compliance_checker` on, the core first evaluates the Rego policies from Langfuse with OPA against the final plan’s `show -json`, deterministically: `general/policies/compliance` and the `<provider>/policies/compliance` of every provider the root module declares (a provider without one is skipped), in one evaluation. Its `deny` findings block; `warn` findings do not. A policy that cannot be evaluated yields a blocking `policy_unavailable` finding: the check fails closed. Contract: [Compliance policy](../../reference/compliance-policy/). |
| Intent check | Then a second, independent small-model agent reads every request of the session and the raw plan output — not the report JSON — alongside the `general/intent/rules` rules. It judges only whether the plan does what the requests ask (`scope_exceeded`, `scope_incomplete`), not the conventions. It has no repository tools and must answer through its only tool, `report_intent_findings`: rule id, severity, resource, message, suggested fix. Both parts' findings, each tagged with its `source` (`opa` or `intent`), are merged into one report, stored like any other artifact, at `compliance/check-<token>.json` with a `compliance_checks` row holding the verdict, so the session detail and the portal can show them. |
| Verdict in code | The model reports findings only, never a verdict: the merged report computes `passed` from the severities, and fails when either part has an `error` or `critical` finding. |
| Lock or release, then pin | The handler first writes `is_blocked`, which decides whether apply and pull-request merge are available, and notifies on failure; only then does the validated workspace with `session.plan` become the session’s pinned plan, replacing any earlier pin. A failed lock write therefore leaves the round unpinned. Configuration, exact formula and effect: [Compliance gate](#compliance). |

/* Progressive enhancement for the block above. Guarded so that a page holding
   several diagrams runs this once, and deferred to DOMContentLoaded because a
   parse-time script cannot yet see the diagrams below it. */
(function () {
  if (window.__archifyEmbed) return
  window.__archifyEmbed = true

  /* The viewer's own interactive chrome. Its toolbar and zoom bar are
     position:fixed, so they always reach the bottom of whatever viewport the
     iframe gives them -- measuring them would make the height measurement
     below a fixpoint that can never shrink. Same selector list as
     docs/diagrams/capture-png.mjs, which hides them instead; here they stay
     visible and are only excluded from the measurement. */
